title: Repeatable read keeps one snapshot
setup:
create table accounts (id int primary key, owner text not null, balance int not null);
insert into accounts values (1, 'Asha', 100), (2, 'Ben', 100);

events.sql: select balance from accounts where id = 1
events.note: B's snapshot is taken by its first query: Asha has 100.

events.sql: update accounts set balance = 150 where id = 1
events.note: A, in autocommit mode, changes it to 150 and commits at once.

events.sql: select balance from accounts where id = 1
events.note: B still sees 100. Every query in a repeatable read transaction sees the same snapshot.

events.sql: update accounts set balance = balance + 10 where id = 1
events.note: B tries to change a row that was changed after its snapshot. PostgreSQL refuses rather than silently overwrite A's change; the application must retry the whole transaction.
events.error: could not serialize access due to concurrent update
